1 فَأَمَ , [or فَأَمَ العُشْبَ, as is shown by an ex. in the S and TA,] aor.
فَاَ^َ , [inf. n. فَأْمٌ, TK,] He (a camel) filled his mouth with herbage; (IAar, S, K;) as also فَئِمَ, (K, TA,) like فَرِحَ; (TA; [in the CK فَأَّمَ;]) and ↓ تَفَآءَمَ . (AA, T, K, TA.) ―
-b2- And فَأَمَ, (T,) or فَأَمَ مِنَ المَآءِ, aor. as above, (K,) He satisfied his thirst with drinking of water. (T, K.) ―
-b3- And فَأَمَ فِى الشَّرَابِ He drank with his mouth, not with his hand nor with any other thing, a gulp, or a draught, (نَفَسًا,) of the wine, or beverage; (T, TA;) said of a man: (TA:) app. from أَفْأَمَ signifying “ he filled ” a vessel: and صَأَمَ signifies the same. (T, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 4.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
